# Human Approvals Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that every approval gate has complete, unambiguous and enforceable decision semantics.
**Created**: 2026-10-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [ADRs](../../../docs/adr/README.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Item tags**: `[Mandatory]` means the criterion derives from the constitution, an approved requirement, or an accepted ADR or ruling. `[Optional]` means it concerns an enhancement. `[Dnn]` refers to a detection from the checklist brief; the detection map is in [../gates/release-evidence-gates.md](../gates/release-evidence-gates.md). Post-implementation evidence checks are in that gates file, not here. Every item is unchecked, including `[Optional]` items, so `/speckit-implement` reports this file as incomplete until a reviewer marks it.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the complete list of mandatory approval gates specified with the required role for each? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-001; Plan §5.1] [D06] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK002 Are approve, reject with reason, escalate and timeout outcomes defined for every gate? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-002; CON III] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK003 Is binding of approvals to specific artifact versions specified, with refusal of approvals for superseded versions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-004] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK004 Is revocation of approvals on replanning specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-ORC-021] [D21] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK005 Are resume preconditions specified separately for timeout and non-timeout safe-stops? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-014, §A-016] [D20] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the final-submission and repository release sign-off gates specified, together with the artifact that records approver and timestamp? [Gap, Plan §5.2; Governance §6] [D31] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is it explicitly stated that no response, a timeout or an agent action can never produce an approval? [Clarity, Spec §FR-GOV-002, §FR-GOV-014, §SC-004] [D15] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the rework bound quantified (PVT-013 = 2), with the outcome when it is exceeded? [Measurability, Spec §FR-GOV-016] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "escalate" specified beyond recording (who decides next, whether the deadline changes)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-GOV-002; Spec §CST-008 deferrable item 4] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the demonstration gate-timeout value specified, and required to be recorded on the run? [Clarity, PVT-005; Plan §6.1] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK011 Is per-risk acceptance at G-RELEASE quantified by naming the severities that must be accepted individually? [Measurability, Plan §5.1; gate-decision.schema.json accepted_risks] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the treatment of scripted decisions (tests only, labeled, excluded from scenario evidence) specified? [Clarity, PD-006; ADR-016] [D23] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Are the release-decision semantics (`not_ready` → `FAILED`, no rework) consistent across spec US-4, plan §5.3, ADR-016, workflow-graph.v2.yaml and gate-decision.schema.json 2.0.0? [Consistency, Human Gate 4; CR-002] [Mandatory]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Is application of a duplicate decision submission specified as at most once? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-ORC-028] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK015 Is material-risk acceptance specified for risks identified outside G-RELEASE (for example at G-SECURITY)? [Coverage, Plan §5.2] [Optional]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- `[Gap]` = the requirement is missing; `[Ambiguity]` = the term or rule needs a definition; `[Conflict]` = two sources disagree; `[Assumption]` = relies on an unvalidated assumption
